problem:
Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A.$ Find the decoupling matrix of the differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$

For this distinct, clarified recovery request, let $P=(v_1\ v_2)$ contain the two given eigenvectors as its columns in that exact order, with their shown scales unchanged. Define the new coordinates by $u=P^{-1}x$. Find the exact matrix $D=P^{-1}$ in $u=Dx$. Match an unchanged displayed choice. The original generic wording leaves the coordinate direction and eigenvector scales unspecified; do not treat its decoupling matrix as unique.
